name: Strategy players · starter cohort
description: 24 fictional adult profiles, informed by game mechanics and research dimensions. A transparent starting hypothesis, not a measured audience sample.
population: English-speaking adult PC players interested in macro RTS, automation, or systems-heavy strategy games.

sources.title: Quantic Foundry gamer motivation model
sources.notes: Primary research describes motivation dimensions and game-audience profiles. Used to choose research dimensions only; does not establish these segment weights or individual profiles.

sources.title: Factorio official gameplay overview
sources.notes: Grounds references to automation, infrastructure, resources and combat in actual game mechanics. Does not measure player preferences.

sources.title: Age of Empires IV official overview
sources.notes: Grounds real-time strategy examples. No population share is inferred from this product page.

segments.label: Automation builders
segments.description: Enjoy planning and optimizing production systems.

segments.label: Competitive strategists
segments.description: Enjoy economic timing, opponents and large tactical confrontations.

segments.label: Systems explorers
segments.description: Enjoy discovering interacting mechanics and long-term progression.

segments.label: Social strategy players
segments.description: Enjoy shared goals, readable systems and playing with friends.

personas.label: Automation builder 01
personas.background: Builds elaborate resource networks in Factorio. Enjoys untangling bottlenecks more than fast reactions; plays solo on weekends.

personas.label: Automation builder 02
personas.background: Plays both factory games and RTS campaigns. Likes seeing an economy turn into a large army, but dislikes constant micromanagement.

personas.label: Automation builder 03
personas.background: Returns to long-running automation saves. Enjoys designing resilient transport networks and recovering when production breaks.

personas.label: Automation builder 04
personas.background: Usually plays cooperative building games. Values clear production chains and steady progress with a small group of friends.

personas.label: Automation builder 05
personas.background: Likes efficiency challenges and compact industrial layouts. Experiments with unusual solutions instead of following optimized guides.

personas.label: Automation builder 06
personas.background: Prefers large, visible industrial scale and extensive technology trees. Interested in a campaign that moves from mining to orbital industry.

personas.label: Competitive strategist 01
personas.background: Plays ranked RTS matches regularly. Enjoys scouting, expansion timing and converting an economic advantage into decisive combat.

personas.label: Competitive strategist 02
personas.background: Grew up playing Age of Empires and likes faction variety. Prefers strategic adaptation over memorizing long sequences of hotkeys.

personas.label: Competitive strategist 03
personas.background: Mostly plays team RTS matches. Enjoys defending allies and coordinating large attacks after a deliberate economic buildup.

personas.label: Competitive strategist 04
personas.background: Follows competitive strategy games but plays casually. Wants readable battles and understandable counters without excessive clicking.

personas.label: Competitive strategist 05
personas.background: Enjoys RTS campaigns and skirmishes against AI. Likes large bases and terrain that creates meaningful offensive choices.

personas.label: Competitive strategist 06
personas.background: Enjoys testing unusual macro strategies. Likes games that reward logistics disruption and protecting important infrastructure.

personas.label: Systems explorer 01
personas.background: Plays systems-heavy strategy games for discovery. Enjoys finding interactions between technology, resources and geography.

personas.label: Systems explorer 02
personas.background: Interested in science-fiction worlds and space logistics. Often explores games slowly before trying competitive modes.

personas.label: Systems explorer 03
personas.background: Likes long campaigns with multiple viable strategies. Prefers a clear sense of progression and meaningful setbacks.

personas.label: Systems explorer 04
personas.background: Enjoys building underground infrastructure and adapting to limited resources. Experiments freely and seldom follows guides.

personas.label: Systems explorer 05
personas.background: Plays strategy games with friends and enjoys learning unfamiliar mechanics together. Space expansion is interesting when it changes strategy.

personas.label: Systems explorer 06
personas.background: Likes simulation depth, coherent resource rules and emergent outcomes. Wants mistakes to have understandable consequences.

personas.label: Social strategy player 01
personas.background: Plays cooperative strategy games once a week with friends. Values understandable goals and room for players with different skill levels.

personas.label: Social strategy player 02
personas.background: Mostly enjoys relaxed multiplayer building. Likes contributing through resource production while friends handle combat.

personas.label: Social strategy player 03
personas.background: Prefers team-based RTS matches over solo ranked play. Enjoys coordinating roles and planning a shared economy.

personas.label: Social strategy player 04
personas.background: Alternates between strategy campaigns and cooperative games. Likes distinct responsibilities and clear feedback about progress.

personas.label: Social strategy player 05
personas.background: Plays with a small mixed-experience group. Will learn complex systems if early sessions are approachable and teammates can help.

personas.label: Social strategy player 06
personas.background: Enjoys long weekend strategy sessions. Prefers big collaborative projects and memorable battles over frequent short matches.

assumptions: Segment weights are illustrative hypotheses, not measured market shares.
All profiles are synthetic; cited sources support research dimensions or game facts, not individual biographies.
Age, language, playtime and platform distribution are assumed.
Profiles were constructed without candidate-name preferences; replace or expand them using audience evidence before relying on results.
